title: Threadline Chat - Harbor Task Rework QC
subtitle: Working-folder review after tab-scoped sessions, direct messages, richer seed data, and thread UX changes.
note: Scope is threadline-chat only. Harbor Oracle had not run when this tracker was generated; evidence is local API, Playwright, Linux-container, static, and packaging validation.

tasks.name: Threadline
tasks.headline: All eight prior findings remain fixed; one pre-existing visible thread-participant gap was found and fixed during this review. No open P0-P3 findings remain before Oracle.

findings.what: Prior finding: committed browser state was not proven across a post-grading restart.
findings.why: A persistence requirement could have passed without testing the actual restart boundary.
findings.impact: A volatile model implementation could receive credit.
findings.fix: Retain the logical SQLite snapshot comparison before and after the post-grading restart.
findings.action: No action. The restart gate still controls the final reward.

findings.what: Prior finding: API checks could pass while visible edit, delete, reaction, pin, and membership controls were absent.
findings.why: That would grade backend equivalents instead of the requested product surface.
findings.impact: A half-built interface could score too highly.
findings.fix: Keep visible positive-control interactions and reserve request replay for trust-boundary probes.
findings.action: No action. The browser rubric still names the required interaction path.

findings.what: Prior finding: reply links targeted only the parent and same-document navigation did not open the exact thread reply.
findings.why: The copied-link workflow did not reach its promised target.
findings.impact: Oracle could fail the exact deep-link criterion.
findings.fix: Retain parent/thread/reply identifiers and shared startup/hash navigation.
findings.action: No action. The exact-target implementation remains present.

findings.what: Prior finding: reusing a client id against another channel or parent could return an unrelated message.
findings.why: Idempotency was not bound to the original operation target.
findings.impact: Cross-target replay could return misleading success.
findings.fix: Retain channel and parent consistency checks before returning a duplicate.
findings.action: No action. Golden API smoke confirms cross-channel and cross-parent rejection.

findings.location: tests/rubric/browser/browser.toml: status, version, deletion, and history wording
findings.what: Prior finding: criteria required golden-specific status codes, initial versions, and display conventions.
findings.why: Correct alternative implementations could be rejected.
findings.impact: The score could measure Oracle shape instead of the instruction.
findings.fix: Retain behavior-based wording and discover versions and routes from the live app.
findings.action: No action. Current criteria remain implementation-neutral where the instruction permits alternatives.

findings.what: Prior finding: shell line endings and dependency fallback could make Linux execution unreliable.
findings.why: Windows checkout or non-lockfile install could break or drift the golden setup.
findings.impact: The task could fail before grading application behavior.
findings.fix: Keep shell files LF-pinned, use npm ci fallback, and exclude runtime and author-only artifacts.
findings.action: No action. Linux container solve and API smoke pass; archive hygiene passes.

findings.what: Prior finding: shared cookies prevented two ordinary tabs from remaining signed in as different users.
findings.why: The required two-tab collaboration workflow could not be verified in one browser context.
findings.impact: Login, live collaboration, and logout isolation checks could fail or require verifier workarounds.
findings.fix: Use server-backed tokens stored per tab in sessionStorage and revoke only the active token on logout.
findings.action: No action. Playwright confirms independent reload, logout, and account switching in same-context tabs.

findings.location: solution/app: direct messages, thread affordance, seed, and layout
findings.what: Prior finding: one-to-one messages were absent, thread creation was hidden, seed data was sparse, and the thread layout used the wrong grid column.
findings.why: Core Slack-style workflows were inaccessible or visually unfinished.
findings.impact: The golden would not satisfy the expanded product contract.
findings.fix: Retain unique participant-only DMs, visible Start a thread controls, richer seed conversations, and explicit channel/thread columns.
findings.action: No action. API, desktop, live two-tab, and mobile checks pass.

findings.what: The instruction requires parent messages to show participating users, but the visible summary showed only reply count and latest time even though the API supplied replyParticipants.
findings.why: A required visible thread detail was present in data but omitted from rendering.
findings.impact: Oracle could fairly fail thread metadata despite correct reply storage.
findings.fix: Render participant names between reply count and latest reply time, while preserving Start a thread for parents without replies.
findings.action: No action. The clean browser rerun passes after the rendering fix.

blocks.title: Release gate
items: Run exactly one Harbor Oracle trial next; run the configured model once only if Oracle reward is exactly 1.0.

blocks.title: Validated surface
items: 24 unique binary criteria and 24 matching feature-map records; total weight 34.0.
Golden API smoke passes identity, authorization, idempotency, stale writes, moderation, threads, mentions, reactions, pins, DMs, webhooks, audit, and logout replay.
Playwright passes same-context two-user login, reload isolation, live DM/thread delivery, visible logout, account switching, and 390x844 mobile layout.
Docker environment build, Linux solve, clean seed, package parsing, reward floor, BaseException handling, and upload-zip hygiene pass.
